vulnerability.root_cause: The function copies an attacker-controlled input into a 16-byte stack destination ([rbp-0x20]) via helper_copy at 0x102cbb0 without validating the input length, allowing writes past the 16-byte buffer and corrupting the stack canary and saved frame.

security_invariants: No write may occur beyond the 16-byte destination buffer [rbp-0x20].
The stack canary at [rbp-8] must remain intact and match fs:[0x28] at function exit.
The destination must be NUL-terminated within capacity (at most 15 bytes plus NUL).
Only direct calls to helper_copy (0x102cbb0) and puts (0x108a31c) are permitted; no syscalls, indirect jumps, or privileged instructions.
Function must terminate with ret preserving x86_64 SysV calling convention.

repair.strategy: Bound the copy length to capacity-1 (15) bytes before invoking helper_copy, ensuring NUL termination within the 16-byte destination; reject or truncate inputs that do not fit while preserving normal behavior for valid inputs.
repair.failure_behavior: For oversized inputs, do not overflow the buffer; either truncate to 15 bytes plus NUL or return without copying, keeping exit code 0 and no crash.
repair.expected_behavior: Valid short inputs (e.g. 'hi') are copied and printed via puts producing 'hi\n' with exit code 0; oversized inputs (64, 256 bytes) do not crash, exit code 0, and stack canary remains valid.

security_conditions: Stack canary check at 0x102cba0 passes (no jne taken to 0x102cbab).
regression_conditions: Calling convention preserved; ret at function end.

note: baseline is deterministic; AI target assembly is accepted only by native/qemu PoC+regression. baseline_target_strict calls repair_any(target=<case target>, require_target=True) and records the resolved target_scope plus target_in_scope (every produced action inside the target; empty action lists are not in scope). baseline_target_aware receives the same target/capacity hint; ai_blind uses the public AI path without target. allow_calls only permits direct calls already present in the target function.
evaluation_note: deterministic baselines run on the host; PoC evaluation and the unstripped x86-64 target execution run in the Linux guest (Lima) via the poc/guest runner. Provider prompts/responses are never stored.
